topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture series, outlines student learning outcomes, and sets the clinical and biological scope of the course.

topics.label: Biological foundations and experimental models of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how cancer develops through accumulated genetic alterations and disrupted tissue differentiation programs, as well as the experimental models used to study these cellular changes.

topics.label: Invasion, metastasis, and histological progression of tumors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the pathological mechanisms of tumor invasion and metastasis, illustrated by the stepwise histological progression from benign adenoma to malignant adenocarcinoma.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and mechanisms of clinical harm
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the classification conventions for benign and malignant tumors and explain how both types cause patient morbidity and mortality.

topics.label: Comparative tumor incidence in humans and animals
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze patterns of tumor incidence across human organ systems and diverse animal species as manifestations of multicellular differentiation.

topics.label: Cancer screening principles and modalities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the clinical rationale, histological indicators, and practical limitations of screening programs for various cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical session reminders
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a summary review of learning outcomes and reminders for upcoming practical sessions.
